title: Hebrews Chapter 8 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 8 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 8 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 8.

questions.question: In Hebrews 8, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A high priest set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
The command to make all things according to the pattern shewed to Moses
High priests offering gifts according to the law
questions.correctAnswer: A high priest set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 states first about the high priest set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens before mentioning other things.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:2, what kind of tabernacle does the Lord pitch?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 explicitly says the Lord pitched the true tabernacle, not made by man.

questions.question: What is every high priest ordained to do according to Hebrews 8:3?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:3 states that every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices.

questions.question: Why must the man mentioned in Hebrews 8:3 have something to offer?
options: Because every high priest must offer gifts and sacrifices
Because he was chosen by Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Because every high priest must offer gifts and sacrifices
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:3 explains the necessity of having something to offer since every high priest offers gifts and sacrifices.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:4, why would the man not be a priest if he were on earth?
options: Because there are priests who offer gifts according to the law
Because he is not from the tribe of Levi
Because the tabernacle is in heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Because there are priests who offer gifts according to the law
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:4 says if he were on earth he would not be a priest since priests already offer gifts according to the law.

questions.question: Who served as an example and shadow of heavenly things as mentioned in Hebrews 8:5?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:5 states that Moses was admonished of God to make the tabernacle as a shadow and example of heavenly things.

questions.question: What did God command Moses to ensure when making the tabernacle according to Hebrews 8:5?
options: That all things be made according to the pattern shewed to him in the mount
That the tabernacle be built quickly
That the tabernacle be made of gold
questions.correctAnswer: That all things be made according to the pattern shewed to him in the mount
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:5 records God’s command to Moses to make all things according to the pattern shown on the mount.

questions.question: Where is the high priest set according to Hebrews 8:1?
options: On the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: On the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 states the high priest is set at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.

questions.question: What role does the man mentioned in Hebrews 8:2 serve?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 describes the man as a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tabernacle.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:4, why is the man not a priest on earth?
options: Because there are priests who offer gifts according to the law
Because he is not from the tribe of Levi
Because he does not offer sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Because there are priests who offer gifts according to the law
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:4 states that if he were on earth he would not be a priest because priests on earth offer gifts according to the law.

questions.question: What did Moses receive from God when he was about to make the tabernacle, according to Hebrews 8:5?
options: Admonishment to make all things according to the pattern shewed to him
Instructions to build a new city
A command to lead the people into battle
A vision of the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: Admonishment to make all things according to the pattern shewed to him
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:5 says Moses was admonished by God to build the tabernacle exactly as the pattern shown to him on the mount.

questions.question: The high priest is described as being set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 states explicitly that the high priest is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.

questions.question: The tabernacle mentioned in Hebrews 8 is described as the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 clearly says the tabernacle is the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched, not man.

questions.question: Hebrews 8 states that the high priest offers sacrifices on earth just like the Levitical priests.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:4 says if he were on earth he would not be a priest, because priests on earth offer gifts according to the law, implying this high priest does not offer sacrifices on earth.

questions.question: Hebrews 8 says Moses was commanded by God to make the tabernacle according to his own design without any pattern shown to him.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:5 states Moses was admonished to make all things according to the pattern shewed to him in the mount, not by his own design.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 8 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 8 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What is Jesus described as in Hebrews 8:1?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 states, 'We have such an high priest,' referring to Jesus as our high priest.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 8:6 say about the ministry of Jesus?
options: It is less than the old covenant
It is a more excellent ministry
It is only for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: It is a more excellent ministry
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6 mentions that Jesus has 'obtained a more excellent ministry,' indicating its superiority.

questions.question: What is the better covenant that Jesus mediates according to Hebrews 8:6?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6 describes Jesus as 'the mediator of a better covenant,' emphasizing its superiority over the old covenant.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:7, why is a second covenant necessary?
options: There was no need for a second covenant
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:7 states, 'For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second,' indicating the faults in the first covenant.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 8:8 promise about the new covenant?
options: It will be made with Gentiles
It will be made with the house of Israel and Judah
It is the same as the old covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It will be made with the house of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:8 states, 'I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,' highlighting the specific groups involved.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 8:9 say about the old covenant?
options: It was not followed by the people
questions.correctAnswer: It was not followed by the people
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:9 mentions that 'they continued not in my covenant,' indicating the failure of the people to uphold it.

questions.question: What will God do with His laws according to Hebrews 8:10?
options: He will write them on stone tablets
He will put them into their minds and hearts
questions.correctAnswer: He will put them into their minds and hearts
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 states, 'I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts,' showing the internalization of God's laws.

questions.question: In practical terms, how should Christians view God's laws according to Hebrews 8:10?
questions.explanation: The promise of having laws in our minds and hearts suggests that they should guide our daily living as Christians.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 8:10 imply about the relationship between God and His people?
options: He will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people
It will be based on fear
questions.correctAnswer: He will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 emphasizes a close, covenant relationship with God, indicating a deep connection between Him and His people.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 8:2 tell us about Jesus' role?
options: He is a minister of the true tabernacle
He is a teacher of the law
questions.correctAnswer: He is a minister of the true tabernacle
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 describes Jesus as 'A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle,' indicating His unique role.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:3, what is necessary for every high priest?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:3 states, 'For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices,' indicating their main duty.

questions.question: Does Hebrews 8:4 suggest that Jesus could serve as a priest on earth?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:4 indicates that 'if he were on earth, he should not be a priest,' implying that His priesthood is of a different order.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 8:6 states that Jesus is the mediator of a worse covenant.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6 states that Jesus is the mediator of a better covenant, not a worse one.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 8:7 says the first covenant was without fault.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:7 indicates that the first covenant had faults, which is why a second covenant was necessary.

questions.question: True or False: The new covenant mentioned in Hebrews 8:8 is made with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:8 clearly states that a new covenant will be made with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 8 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 8.

questions.question: What will every man not teach his neighbor according to Hebrews 8:11?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 8:11 states, 'And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.'

questions.question: What will God be merciful to according to Hebrews 8:12?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 8:12 states, 'For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.'

questions.question: What is made old when God establishes a new covenant according to Hebrews 8:13?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 8:13 states, 'In that he saith, A new covenant, he hath made the first old.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:12, what will God remember no more?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 8:12 states that God will be merciful and will not remember their sins and iniquities anymore.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'from the least to the greatest' in Hebrews 8:11?
options: Only the greatest will know God
Only the least will not know God
questions.explanation: This is correct because it emphasizes that all individuals, regardless of status, will have direct knowledge of the Lord.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'covenant' in Hebrews 8:13 imply?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for covenant (diatheke) implies an unbreakable bond, which is crucial in understanding God's promises.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Hebrews 8:10-12 when stating the new covenant will not require teaching?
questions.explanation: This is correct as the structure of the passages employs parallelism, emphasizing the contrast between the old and new covenants.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the new covenant in Hebrews 8:8?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 speaks of a new covenant, connecting directly to Hebrews 8:8, where the author cites God making a new covenant.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of knowing the Lord in Hebrews 8:11?
questions.explanation: John 17:3 states that eternal life is knowing the only true God, fulfilling the promise made in Hebrews 8:11.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Hebrews 8:11?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 states, 'For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days,' which directly precedes verse 11.

questions.question: What comes immediately after Hebrews 8:12?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:13 follows immediately after verse 12, discussing the implications of the new covenant.

questions.question: In the context of Hebrews 8:6, what does 'better promises' refer to?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Hebrews 8:6 indicates that a better covenant is established upon better promises compared to the old system.

questions.question: The phrase 'I will put my laws into their mind' in Hebrews 8:10 indicates what kind of relationship?
questions.explanation: This is correct because the promise indicates a transformative internal relationship with God's laws as indicated in Hebrews 8:10.

questions.question: True or False: The new covenant mentioned in Hebrews 8 is a reiteration of the old covenant.
questions.explanation: This is correct because the new covenant is fundamentally different and replaces the old, as indicated in Hebrews 8:13.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 8:12, God will remember the iniquities of His people.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Hebrews 8:12 states, 'I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.'

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 8 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 8 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 8:2 teach about God's nature in relation to the sanctuary?
options: God established a true sanctuary in heaven, not made by human hands
God's sanctuary is entirely a human construction
God dwells only in earthly temples
God's presence is limited to the tabernacle Moses built
questions.correctAnswer: God established a true sanctuary in heaven, not made by human hands
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 states that Jesus ministers in the 'true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man,' emphasizing God's divine establishment of a heavenly sanctuary, distinct from earthly ones.

questions.question: What doctrine about the priesthood does Hebrews 8:4 teach concerning Jesus’ earthly ministry?
options: Jesus cannot be a priest on earth because there are priests who offer gifts by the law
Jesus served as a high priest offering sacrifices in the earthly temple
Jesus did not serve as a priest at all
Jesus was a priest only temporarily on earth
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus cannot be a priest on earth because there are priests who offer gifts by the law
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:4 explains that if Jesus were on earth, He could not be a priest because priests offering gifts according to the law already existed on earth, indicating His priesthood is heavenly.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the covenant is taught in Hebrews 8:7?
options: The first covenant was flawed, necessitating a second, better covenant
The first covenant was perfect and eternal
There is no need for a new covenant
The second covenant is identical to the first
questions.correctAnswer: The first covenant was flawed, necessitating a second, better covenant
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:7 states that if the first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second, indicating the first covenant's imperfection necessitated a new one.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 8:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:12 declares God will be merciful and will remember sins no more, showing the divine attribute of mercy.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 8:10 most clearly demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 records God promising to put His laws into their minds and write them on their hearts, affirming His faithfulness to establish and keep His covenant.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 8:1 connect to the wider biblical theme of Christ’s exaltation?
options: It affirms Christ’s position at the right hand of God’s throne, fulfilling Psalm 110
It limits Christ’s authority to earth
It describes Christ as a mere prophet
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Christ’s position at the right hand of God’s throne, fulfilling Psalm 110
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 states the high priest is seated at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven, connecting with Psalm 110’s Messianic prophecy about Christ’s exaltation.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 8:8 relate to the prophetic promises of Jeremiah concerning the new covenant?
options: It directly quotes Jeremiah’s promise of a new covenant with Israel and Judah
It promotes a return to the Mosaic covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It directly quotes Jeremiah’s promise of a new covenant with Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:8 cites God’s promise of a new covenant with Israel and Judah, referencing Jeremiah 31:31-34, thus connecting the text to Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 8:6 and 8:13 teach about Christ’s priesthood and covenant?
options: Christ mediates a better covenant with a more excellent ministry, making the first covenant obsolete
Christ’s ministry is inferior to the Mosaic priesthood
The first covenant remains fully valid alongside Christ’s ministry
Christ’s priesthood replaces the need for any covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Christ mediates a better covenant with a more excellent ministry, making the first covenant obsolete
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6 speaks of Christ’s superior ministry and better covenant, while 8:13 states that by calling it a new covenant, the first is made old and ready to vanish, showing the new covenant’s superiority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 8:10 and 8:11 teach about the internal transformation in the new covenant?
options: God will write His laws on hearts and minds, resulting in universal knowledge of Him
The new covenant requires external adherence only
Only priests will know God intimately
The new covenant abolishes the law completely
questions.correctAnswer: God will write His laws on hearts and minds, resulting in universal knowledge of Him
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:10 promises God will put His laws into minds and hearts, and 8:11 states all will know the Lord, highlighting internal transformation and universal knowledge under the new covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 8:3 and 8:5 teach about the nature of the earthly priesthood and tabernacle?
options: The earthly priesthood and tabernacle are shadows and examples of heavenly realities
The earthly priesthood offers perfect and final sacrifices
The tabernacle Moses built was the ultimate sanctuary
The earthly priesthood and tabernacle are unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: The earthly priesthood and tabernacle are shadows and examples of heavenly realities
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:3 notes the high priest offers gifts and sacrifices, while 8:5 teaches that Moses' tabernacle was made as a pattern or shadow of heavenly things, indicating an earthly copy of a heavenly reality.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Hebrews 8:8-10 merely repeats the old covenant without change. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches a new covenant distinct from the old, with internal law-writing and a renewed relationship
It confirms the old covenant remains fully valid and unaltered
It denies any covenant with Israel
It advocates returning to the covenant made at Sinai
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches a new covenant distinct from the old, with internal law-writing and a renewed relationship
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:8-10 quotes God promising a new covenant not like the covenant made with their fathers, with laws written on hearts, indicating a fundamentally different and internalized covenant.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 8:9 teach regarding human faithfulness and covenant relationship?
options: The people did not continue in the old covenant, leading God to disregard them
The people perfectly kept the old covenant
God abandoned the covenant despite their faithfulness
The covenant was unconditional and never broken
questions.correctAnswer: The people did not continue in the old covenant, leading God to disregard them
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:9 states God took them out of Egypt but they did not continue in His covenant, so He regarded them not, showing human failure to keep covenant obligations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Hebrews 8:1 regarding Christ’s current status?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:1 declares Christ is seated at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven, signifying His sovereign rule and supreme authority.

questions.question: What narrative arc does Hebrews 8:13 continue concerning the old covenant’s obsolescence?
options: It teaches the old covenant is aging and ready to vanish away with the new covenant’s establishment
It affirms the old covenant’s eternal validity
It advocates restoring the old covenant practices
It denies any difference between old and new covenants
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the old covenant is aging and ready to vanish away with the new covenant’s establishment
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:13 explicitly states that by calling it a new covenant, the first is made old and is ready to disappear, emphasizing the old covenant’s obsolescence.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus’ mediation is taught in Hebrews 8:6 regarding salvation?
options: Jesus is the mediator of a better covenant established on better promises
Jesus’ mediation is inferior to the Mosaic covenant
Jesus does not act as a mediator
Jesus mediates the same covenant as Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the mediator of a better covenant established on better promises
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:6 teaches that Jesus has obtained a superior ministry as the mediator of a better covenant founded on better promises, highlighting His unique role in salvation.
